text:
New Jersey arrives at Vegas with its four-game winning streak snapped, a 5-2 loss at COL two days ago, and tonight is the last stop of a three-game road trip. It's the third game in four nights for the Devils, who are 4-1-0 in their last five. Vegas, 2-2-1 over that span, snapped a three-game winless run with a 4-1 win over OTT, in which Raphael Lavoie scored his first NHL goal. The Golden Knights are without Parker Wotherspoon, and Brayden McNabb plays his 900th NHL game.

Our numbers see little between them: NJD has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, VGK 55%, and our model has it 3.08 to 2.95 for the Devils. New Jersey creates 3.51 expected goals per 60 and allows 2.51, against 3.48 and 2.64 for Vegas. The Devils are better than their record, with finishing and goaltending costing them. Vegas takes more penalties (3.36 a game to 2.38) but kills them well. In net, projected starter Connor Hellebuyck has 0.71 goals saved above expected in one start (3.43 last year). Projected Adin Hill is at -0.78 this season and -15.02 last.

Jack Hughes is our pick to score at 35%, and Nico Hischier, with seven goals in 12 games, sits at 30%. Mitch Marner brings an eight-game point streak for Vegas, and Mark Stone is our top Golden Knights goal pick at 34%.
